articles.title: I expect you to cry: what the James Bond actors may face at the final audition
articles.summary: Jack Lowden, Callum Turner and Josh O’Connor are rumoured to be the final candidates taking screentests this weekend. So how can they best prepare? And who is likely to triumph? This weekend, the identity of the next James Bond is finally expected to be known – to the insiders, at least.
body: To say it has been a long time coming is an understatement. It is five years since Daniel Craig was killed in a hail of missiles at the end of No Time to Die, and in that time – even long before it – a swarm of actors have been tipped to replace him, only to age out of the role due to a combination of indecisiveness and cutthroat backstage corporate shenanigans. Whoever is declared to be 007 will be joining the franchise after what is likely to be the longest fallow period in the franchise’s 64-year history.
As such, this is kind of a big weekend. Let’s run through what we know so far.

If three actors are to screen test for Bond this weekend, then they are Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor and Jack Lowden. If there are more – some outlets state that one other actor might be participating, others two – then they won’t include Jack O’Connell or Jacob Elordi, who are both out of the race for one reason or another.

The identity of the other actors are not yet known. Let’s take an uneducated guess and assume that one of them is a Beatle (the best fit is Harris Dickinson) and another one is more famous but less suitable (like Tom Cruise).
points: Jack Lowden, Callum Turner and Josh O’Connor are rumoured to be the final candidates taking screentests this weekend.

articles.title: ‘Fighting an impossible fight is the only way to reclaim dignity’: Lee Chang-dong on class warfare and his searing Oscar contender
articles.summary: The auteur’s new film – a study of labour, capital and the fallout of redundancy – won the grand jury prize at Venice. Telling tales of the disenfranchised is ‘our moral responsibility’, he says. A quintessential 21st-century horror story: a private equity firm has set its sights on your company.
body: In 2009, workers at Ssangyong Motors company protested against plans to lay off between 37 and 43% of the workforce, staging a historic 77-day strike and occupation of the factory that was eventually broken up by riot police. “Until that point in time in Korea, labourers’ rights were widely accepted,” Lee says, speaking through an interpreter in a central London hotel; “however, afterwards, the basic rights of labourers changed; to the public, they couldn’t be seen as more important than market profitability or corporate competitiveness.”

At the time, Lee shelved the project. “The more I examined the pain of these individuals” – after the violent crackdown on the Ssangyong Motors strike, there were several suicides, and reports of long-term mental health issues – “I constantly asked myself: am I worthy of telling this story? And if I am, how do I tell it? Do I stand close to the workers, or keep my distance?” Later he and his co-writer Oh Jung-mi, wrote “many different” scripts, including one with post-apocalyptic elements, before Oh suggested introducing a character who is a documentary film-maker, thereby finding a way to work in Lee’s ambivalence about his intentions.

articles.title: Taika Waititi’s Star Wars film is the latest to hit the buffers. At some point Lucasfilm is going to have to actually make a movie
articles.summary: Waititi joins a long list of movie-makers who were expected to bring a new direction to the franchise, before the studio appeared to get cold feet. Movie-making these days is a very expensive endeavour.
body: Perhaps this is one of the reasons why Disney-owned Lucasfilm seems to be so terrified of making new Star Wars movies. Since 2019’s The Rise of Skywalker, only one Star Wars film, the aforementioned Mando and Grogu movie, has actually made it into cinemas. But that has not stopped the studio announcing a small armada of other projects – sometimes via press release, more often at various high-profile celebrations, conferences or other corporate jamborees – that have so far failed to reach multiplexes.

This week, Taika Waititi revealed in an interview with Inverse that his proposed Star Wars film, announced six years ago, has been “put on ice”. No clear explanation was offered, but frankly nobody should be surprised. It now joins mooted projects from Patty Jenkins, Kevin Feige and Game of Thrones creators David Benioff and DB Weiss on the list of Star Wars movies that we were once told we were definitely (probably) getting, but that we never actually did. Some, such as Rian Johnson’s proposed trilogy, have spent years receding into the distance, while others – Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy’s film about Rey’s new Jedi order, anyone? – have never been officially cancelled.
points: Waititi joins a long list of movie-makers who were expected to bring a new direction to the franchise, before the studio appeared to get cold feet.

articles.title: ‘Overnight, everything was dead’: the Teesside fisherman turned activist dubbed the Mr Bates of the seas
articles.summary: When thousands of dying crabs washed up on a Yorkshire beach in 2021, Stan Rennie’s livelihood was immediately threatened. Five years later, he’s leading the fight back against toxic ocean pollution – and corporate coverups.
body: It was an otherwise typical day on 25 September 2021 when thousands of dead and dying crustaceans washed up on beaches in Yorkshire and the north-east of England. Early morning walkers and swimmers were aghast to find a sickening carpet of twitching, fitting crabs.

It would be the first but not the last die-off, which would see the disappearance of vast swathes of integral native sea life along an extended stretch of coast, including seal pups. It would also see the decimation of the local fishing industry and, with that, a way of life.

Environmentalists, fishers and ordinary local people wondered what could have possibly caused such a rare catastrophic incident. Meanwhile, hours before – completely coincidentally, the authorities said – a major dredging operation was carried out in the mouth of the River Tees, disturbing sediment where decades earlier highly toxic pollutants from heavy industry had been pumped.

The authorities, after carrying out a series of their own tests, denied there was a causal link, blaming an algae bloom and then, later, a novel pathogen. But those who live and work around the Tees estuary disagreed.

Five years later, he’s leading the fight back against toxic ocean pollution – and corporate coverups.

articles.title: Belgian Series ‘The Inheritance’ Scores Sony Pictures Television Award at Rome’s MIA Market
articles.summary: Belgian TV series “The Inheritance,” about the death of a wealthy widow that ignites a battle over her estate, scored the Sony Pictures Television Award for best drama project at Rome’s MIA Market as its 12th edition wrapped Friday.
body: MIA Development Awards were also handed out to several projects selected across the four categories of the co-production market and pitching forum, with each receiving cash prizes to support their development.

The development award for outstanding animation series project went to “Sophie, if You Are There Give Us a Sign!,” directed by Italy’s Dario Piana, an Italy-Belgium-Spain co-production between Brand-Cross, 20 Pictures to Midnight and Digitoonz Entertainment. The series focuses on a 13-year-old named Sophie, who mourns her grandfather Thomas every day in a Milan cemetery. Her reality is shattered when two mischievous ghost children from the “World Below” perform a forbidden so-called “Vivitic Séance,” accidentally pulling Sophie into this other realm.

The prize for outstanding animated film project went to “All the Softness in the World,” about a Turkish family in 1950s Istanbul that lives in the shadow of an ancient curse, directed by Ayce Kartal and produced by France’s Les Valseurs.

articles.title: Who Should Be the Next James Bond? 25 Picks for the New 007
articles.summary: Ever since Daniel Craig announced that he would be turning in the tuxedo and putting down the martini glass, the race has been on to decide who will be chosen as the next James Bond. The rumor mill has been heating up for years now, but now it’s really down to the wire for the
body: Once “Dune” director Denis Villeneuve was hired to shepherd the next installment, with Steven Knight writing the script, it was off to the races to decide who casting director Nina Gold and Villeneuve would select.

The series’ previous producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael Wilson were clear about three things: The next Bond should be played by a Brit; the next Bond should be young enough to be able to continue in the role for at least 15 years; and the next Bond will be a man, not a woman.

But with Broccoli and Wilson turning over creative control to Amazon MGM, there’s no telling what changes might be in store. Amy Pascal and David Heyman are now producing, and since it’s their first Bond film, any number of changes could be in store. And as Agent 007 knows better than most, rules are meant to be bent, if not broken outright.

For this list, we cast a wide net of actors mostly in the under-40 category — yes, even a couple of women — so sorry to earlier picks like Idris Elba, Henry Cavill and others who have aged out of the running. The most important criteria was whether the actor could bring the necessary gravitas, style and charm to playing Britain’s most famous secret agent.

articles.title: AI Giant Nvidia Invests in Entertainment Startup Higgsfield
articles.summary: Higgsfield, the AI video and image generation company dabbling across both marketing and entertainment spaces, extended its Series B funding round with new investments from Nvidia and the investment firm TCV.
body: “We believe Alex and the Higgsfield team are delivering on a powerful vision at a pace of product velocity and market adoption that we have rarely seen: a radically faster, professional-grade and AI-native mechanism for creators, brand marketers and agencies alike to turn ideas into images and video,” Neil Tolaney, General Partner at TCV, added.

Nvidia has invested in other entertainment-minded AI startups before, including two separate investments in Lionsgate partner Runway. Its Higgsfield investment, Nvidia’s first in the company, comes as the startup has relied on the tech behemoth’s resources to power its platform, where it processes 12 trillion tokens a month across 150 million generations.

“AI factories produce intelligence in the form of tokens and the application layer is where those tokens become useful,” said Rev Lebaredian, Nvidia’s vice president of physical AI simulation, in a statement. “The collaboration between Higgsfield and Nvidia across hardware and software is turning compute into creative work for millions of users and hundreds of the world’s largest brands.”

articles.title: Top 10 Movies That Explain What’s Happening in France Right Now
articles.summary: Amid riots, looting and protests by French students angry at the conditions of their high schools, THR’s Paris-based film critic picks 10 essential movies that shed light on the tensions leading to this moment.
body: “ Plus ça change, plus c’est la même chose ” (“The more things change, the more they stay the same”) is a very French way to describe this phenomenon; the same struggles return with each new generation, whether it’s citoyens fighting the monarchy, Maoists fighting de Gaulle, immigrants from former colonies (and their French-born offspring) fighting police, or students fighting for better schools at a time when their future seems more uncertain than ever.

The movies below, listed in chronological order, depict this long, continuous struggle across multiple viewpoints and time periods, illustrating the extent to which it belongs to French cinema as well as to the French themselves.

articles.title: Final James Bond screen tests to take place this weekend, reports say
articles.summary: Callum Turner and Jack Lowden "appear to be in the mix" of actors doing screen tests for the role.
body: Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Josh O'Connor are among the actors thought to be taking part in final auditions to play James Bond, according to reports.

Screen tests are said to be taking place this weekend, possibly as early as Friday, according to the Hollywood Reporter, external, with between three and five actors understood to have reached the last stages of the process.
The finalists are said to be taking part in auditions with three components - stunts, camera presence and dialogue.

Deadline reported the screen tests, external had been due take place in early October, but had been delayed by scheduling conflicts, while Variety said Turner and Lowden, external "appear to be in the mix" to replace Daniel Craig.

articles.title: Bravo’s ‘Next Gen’ Goes Franchise With New Atlanta-Based Series
articles.summary: The network announced Friday that 'Next Gen NYC' was renewed for its third season, while revealing a greenlight for the new show based in Georgia; plus, 'Southern Hospitality' and 'In The City' scored season renewals.
body: Bravo ‘s Next Gen is expanding into its own franchise, with the network revealing Friday ahead of Bravo Fan Fest Charleston that Next Gen Atlanta has officially been greenlit.

The announcement marks the first extension to Next Gen NYC, Bravo’s buzzy new entry that debuted in 2025 and featured a cast of children of Housewives, combined with other cast members, a few of which had parents who also had experience in the spotlight. Bravo has not shared any details about who will make up the cast of Next Gen Atlanta.

The logline for Next Gen Atlanta reads, “In a city where hip-hop, sports and entertainment shape the social scene, Next Gen Atlanta follows a new generation of rising personalities making their mark. Some have famous ties, while others are building their reputations from the ground up, but all have big dreams and plenty to prove as they juggle careers, friendships and family dynamics.”

The series is produced by Blink49 Studios with Tara Long, Nadine Rajabi, Mark Ford, Ben Magargel, Salena Rochester and Shari Levine serving as executive producers. Bianca Barnes-Williams, Tiffany Mills and Anne Swan also serve as executive producers. Lauren Nathan serves as co-executive producer.
